rule_summary: Follows FPSC Rule 25-6.065 tiers (T1 <=10 kW, T2 <=100 kW, T3 <=2 MW AC; AC = DC x 0.85). Adds a sizing screen not in the rule: system must be estimated to produce <115% of annual kWh consumption; NEM systems >=50 kW must interconnect three-phase wye. Tier 2 fee $400, Tier 3 fee $1,000; Tier 2 insurance $1M. FPL requires a lockable visible-break manual disconnect for Tier 2 and Tier 3 (waived for inverter-based Tier 1 per rule).
ic_application_fee: Tier 1 $0; Tier 2 $400; Tier 3 $1,000 (plus study charge if required)
external_disconnect: Required for Tier 2 and Tier 3 (adjacent to meter, lockable); waived Tier 1
non_export_option: Yes for stand-alone batteries: grid-charged storage without renewables submits a Small Generator Interconnection Application; if non-exporting and no utility equipment needed, no interconnection agreement is required
storage_specific_notes: FPL battery policy: battery paired with NEM renewable system is for customer use only and may NOT export to the grid (so battery energy never earns NEM credit); UL 1741 certification required, non-UL batteries must be DC-coupled behind a UL 1741 device; meter placard 'Battery storage utilized in this facility'. Tier 3 batteries reviewed in fast-track study. Stand-alone storage is not 'renewable' under 25-6.065(2)(d) and its output is not net metered. Adding a battery to an existing NEM system: no loss of NEM status stated (FL has no legacy/successor split); interconnection agreement sec. 7 requires a new application/agreement 30 days ahead only if gross power rating increases -- whether an AC-coupled battery counts as a rating increase is Unclear. Policy stated as subject to change.

rule_summary: No AL statewide NEM/interconnection rule; Alabama Power tariffs are the rule (see AL state row). No net metering: exports bought under Rate PAE (<=100 kW) at avoided cost (~4.4-7.7c/kWh by TOU period); Rate Rider RGB capacity reservation charge $5.41/kW-month (secondary) on generator nameplate or RTA 71c/kWh summer 3-5pm alternative. 3-tier DER process: Tier I <=25 kW $0, Tier II <=100 kW $500, Tier III >100 kW $1,000 screen. IEEE 1547-2018/UL 1741-SB; lockable visible-break AC disconnect required.
export_credit_value: Rate PAE TOD option: Jun-Sep 7.44c/kWh (wkdy 10am-9pm CT) / 5.23c; Oct-May 4.86c / 4.41c (rev. eff. April 2023 billings as posted)
ic_application_fee: Tier I $0; Tier II $500; Tier III $1,000 screening (+$10k-$50k if studies)
non_export_option: Yes: Non-Export / Limited-Export Generation defined in DER TIR Guidebook; UL 1741 CRD PCS or UL 3141 power control systems accepted; RGB still applies to non-exporting generation
standby_charge: Rate Rider RGB Capacity Reservation Charge $5.41/kW-month secondary, $4.87/kW-month primary, on nameplate of on-site non-emergency generation; upheld by M.D. Ala. 2026-03-25 (appeal status unverified)
standby_threshold_kw: None (applies to all parallel non-emergency generation)
storage_specific_notes: Storage is a DER under the APC Guidebook (spec sheets must give battery kW, kWh). Adding a battery to an existing PV system is a modification: any addition/removal or inverter change requires a NEW interconnection application and permission to operate before paralleling; SLD must show battery as new and PV as existing. No NEM grandfathering exists to lose, but whether a battery (esp. grid-charged or non-exporting) adds to RGB-billed nameplate kW is Unclear. PAE purchases only energy from a PURPA qualifying facility, so export of grid-charged battery energy under PAE is Unclear/likely not credited. V2G/V2H: normal application, external disconnect and MID required.

rule_summary: Follows FPSC Rule 25-6.065 tiers (T1 <=10 kW, T2 >10-100 kW, T3 >100 kW-2 MW) under Net Metering Rider; utility-set fees: Tier 1 $0, Tier 2 $240, Tier 3 $750 (+ study; results within 60 days). Insurance T1 recommended $100k (not required), T2 $1M, T3 $2M. Tier 2/3 require externally accessible lockable manual AC load-break disconnect (not a breaker) near meter. Service-drop screen: PV rating <=90% of transformer/service rating or customer pays upgrade. Tier 1 PTO usually within 10 business days of completion.
external_disconnect: Required Tier 2 and Tier 3 (visible-break, lockable, labeled Generator Disconnect Switch); not required Tier 1
storage_specific_notes: DEF net-metering tier pages and application do not address batteries (unlike FPL, no published battery-export prohibition found). Whether battery export earns NEM credit, whether grid charging is permitted on a NEM account, and whether adding a battery to an existing NEM system requires a new application: all Unclear from DEF published material. No legacy/successor NEM split in FL, so no grandfathering to lose. DEF runs EnergyWise Home Battery Control DR (see programs).

rule_summary: Follows FPSC Rule 25-6.065 via Rate Schedule NM-1 and Standard Interconnection Agreements (Tier 1 <=10 kW, Tier 2 >10-100 kW, Tier 3 >100 kW-2 MW AC; GPR = DC x 0.85; GPR <=90% of service rating). Utility-set fees: Tier 2 $250 one-time (no charge for any Tier 2 study); Tier 3 $500 + study deposit $3,000 (actual cost, capped $3,000). Insurance T2 $1M, T3 $2M (self-insurance by approval). Visible load-break lockable manual disconnect adjacent to meter required T2/T3. Agreement executed within 30 days (90 if Tier 3 study); PTO notice within 10 business days. Agreements still cite IEEE 1547-2003/UL 1741-2005.
ic_application_fee: Tier 1 $0; Tier 2 $250; Tier 3 $500 + study up to $3,000 (deposit $3,000)
ic_study_trigger_kw: 100 (Tier 3; Tier 2 study at no charge if needed)
external_disconnect: Required Tier 2 and Tier 3 (visible load-break, lockable, exterior adjacent to meter)
storage_specific_notes: Agreements define RGS as renewable generation only; batteries not addressed in NM-1 agreements read. TECO Steps to Connect page reportedly states batteries are interconnected but not net metered (search-snippet only; page could not be loaded, redirect loop) -- implies battery discharge does not earn NEM credit: Unverified. Adding a battery: agreement sec. 7 requires a new application 30 days ahead only for a change in GPR; whether a battery changes GPR is Unclear. No legacy NEM tier to lose in FL.

rule_summary: Municipal; exempt from FPSC Rule 25-6.065 (s. 366.91(6) F.S. requires own program). JEA Distributed Generation Policy eff. 2018-04-01 replaced net metering: monthly netting but exported kWh credited at JEA fuel rate (~3c/kWh at launch) instead of retail; credits accrue through calendar year and remaining balance paid at year end per policy. Systems passing final inspection by 2018-03-31 grandfathered under retired Net Metering Policy (Tiers 1-3, full retail) for 20 years; 10 MW aggregate cap applied to legacy Tier 1-3 net metering. Interconnection via PowerClerk; JEA DER Technical Interconnection & Interoperability Requirements (2025).
nem_aggregate_cap: 10 MW aggregate for legacy Tier 1-3 net metering (closed 2018)
export_credit_value: Exports credited at JEA fuel charge rate (post-2018-04-01 systems); legacy NM systems full retail through 20-yr grandfather
external_disconnect: Required (utility disconnect); separate battery load disconnect if permanently mounted battery(ies) (per JEA DER requirements, search snippet)
storage_specific_notes: Adding a battery to a legacy (pre-4/1/2018) net-metered system: JEA pages state (per search snippet) that a grandfathered NM customer who takes JEA Battery Incentive loses grandfathering and moves to the Distributed Generation (fuel-rate) program -- the retrofit trigger is taking the incentive; whether a self-funded battery retrofit also forfeits grandfathering is Unclear. JEA itself framed batteries as a way to self-consume rather than export at fuel rate (2018 rebate up to $4,000, first 50). jea.com blocks automated fetch (CAPTCHA) so policy text not read directly.

rule_summary: Municipal; own TruNet Solar net metering program (s. 366.91(6) F.S.). Tiers by AC gross power rating mirror FPSC tiers: Tier 1 0-10 kW no fee; Tier 2 >10-100 kW $340; Tier 3 >100 kW-2 MW $1,300. Systems connected/approved by 2025-06-30 grandfathered at full retail through 2045-06-30. Systems interconnected after 2025-06-30: full retail during grace period through 2026-10-31, then Community Solar Energy rate through 2030-06-30, then Retail Levelized Fuel rate. From 2026-11-01 exports credited within the same billing period (no kWh rollover); leftover $ credit carries forward on account. Annual true-up done Dec 2025 plus a final true-up Fall 2026. Sizing: capacity should not exceed home energy needs. MID-TRANSITION: successor rates take effect Nov 2026.
export_credit_value: Legacy (<=2025-06-30): full retail ~10.7c/kWh residential through 2045; new: full retail to 2026-10-31, then Community Solar Energy rate (~4.6c/kWh per program chunk, Secondary) to 2030-06-30, then Retail Levelized Fuel rate
storage_specific_notes: Battery retrofit on legacy system: taking OUC Battery Storage Rebate requires forfeiting TruNet Full Retail Rate (10.7c/kWh) on all exports -- i.e., a rebated battery retrofit loses grandfathering. An add-on PV array does NOT affect grandfathered status (OUC FAQ); whether a self-funded (non-rebate) battery retrofit affects grandfathering is not stated: Unclear. Applications may be solar or solar+battery. Grid-charging rules not published.

rule_summary: Co-op; own Net Metering Rider (Sheet 11.000, eff. 2023-02-01) modeled on FPSC Rule 25-6.065 but with deviations: Tier 3 capped at 1 MW (not 2 MW); net-metered customers billed on a separate flat (non-tiered) Net Metering rate (RS 8.21c/kWh total energy + $22.22 customer charge vs. standard inverted-block rate). Monthly kWh netting; excess kWh carried forward to end of calendar year and paid at LCEC calculated avoided purchased power cost for prior year. Fees: Tier 1 $35 (rule has $0 for IOUs), Tier 2 up to $1,000, Tier 3 $1,000 (+ study up to $2,000 per LCEC fees page). Tier 2 insurance $1M; lockable visible load-break disconnect within 5 ft of meter (Tier 2). GPR <=90% of service/transformer rating. Standby or resale service not permitted under rider.
nem_cap_res_kw: 1000 (Tier 3 max; rule applies 1 MW, not 2 MW)
export_credit_value: 1:1 kWh netting at Net Metering Rider flat rate (RS 8.21c/kWh energy + PCA); year-end excess paid at LCEC avoided purchased power cost (prior year)
ic_application_fee: Tier 1 $35; Tier 2 up to $1,000; Tier 3 $1,000 (+ study fee up to $2,000 if applicable)
external_disconnect: Required Tier 2 (visible load-break, lockable, within 5 ft of meter); Tier 1 not verified
standby_charge: Standby service not permitted under Net Metering Rider
storage_specific_notes: Rider and agreements cover renewable generation systems only; batteries not addressed. Agreement requires a new application 30 days before modifications that increase GPR; whether a battery increases GPR is Unclear. No legacy/successor split at LCEC so no grandfathering to lose. Grid charging/battery export credit: Unclear.

rule_summary: Co-op; own Net Metering Rider and single-form "Interconnection and Parallel Operation of Renewable Distribution Generation" agreement (rev. 10/22/19) instead of FPSC 25-6.065 tiered agreements. Net meter measures delivered and received kWh; excess over the year purchased at year end at the avoided cost of wholesale supplier Seminole Electric Cooperative. Agreement: 1-yr auto-renewing term; co-op may terminate service at its sole discretion or disconnect without notice for safety; access required for WREC and Seminole; no intentional islanding (IEEE 1547). Tier sizes, fees and insurance not stated in agreement; Net Metering Rider text not read.
export_credit_value: Monthly netting (retail); annual excess paid at Seminole Electric avoided cost
storage_specific_notes: WREC solar FAQ treats batteries only as storing excess PV for self-use (battery-backed systems); no statement on battery export credit, grid charging, or retrofit treatment. No legacy/successor split so no grandfathering to lose. Unclear on all storage-specific rules.

rule_summary: Co-op (Sumter Electric Cooperative d/b/a SECO Energy); own Net Metering tariff Sheet 16.4 + Interconnection Agreement Sheets 17.0-17.5 (eff. 2022-04-01) under Seminole Electric wholesale contract. Tiers per 25-6.065 but capped at 1,000 kW AC (not 2 MW); GPR (DC x 0.85) <=90% of service rating. Net billing, not retail NEM: all kWh taken from grid billed at otherwise applicable rate; excess kWh delivered to grid in each billing cycle credited at base cost of power (Schedule PCA) + monthly WPCA factor (wholesale/avoided cost). Credits only to the service behind which system sits. Insurance: none <=10 kW, $1M >10 kW (co-op as additional insured). Lockable manual disconnect separate from meter socket required for all sizes. IEEE 1547 / UL 1741 latest version. AMI bi-directional meter required. PTO within 10 business days.
export_credit_value: Excess kWh each billing cycle credited at Schedule PCA base cost of power + WPCA factor (wholesale power cost), not retail
external_disconnect: Required all tiers (lockable manual disconnect, separate from meter socket, readily accessible)
storage_specific_notes: SECO interconnection agreement explicitly lists "battery storage" among RGS energy sources (rare in FL) -- battery may interconnect under the standard agreement. Because exports are credited at wholesale cost of power in the same billing cycle (net billing), battery self-consumption shifting has value; whether grid-charged battery exports are credited is not addressed: Unclear. Adding a battery: new application required 30 days ahead for any GPR change; whether battery kW counts toward GPR/1 MW cap is Unclear. No legacy tier to lose.

rule_summary: Co-op (Seminole Electric member); own Form IGRG-1 Interconnection Agreement (Sheets 21.0-21.04, eff. 2026-04-30) and "Avoided Cost" net billing program. RGS rated <=1,000 kW AC and should be designed not to exceed member service load consumption; >=20 kW requires engineering pre-approval; GPR (DC x 0.85) <=90% of service entrance rating or co-op transformer kVA, and co-op will not upsize distribution equipment for oversized RGS. Export: excess kWh bought back at current Seminole QF-1 wholesale rate and credited on next bill (not retail). Insurance: $100k for <=10 kW (stricter than FPSC rule), $1M >10 kW. Lockable manual disconnect separate from meter socket required for all sizes. Net meter install $60 trip fee; processing fee at co-op discretion.
nem_cap_res_kw: 1000 (agreement max; sized to load; >=20 kW pre-approval)
export_credit_value: Excess kWh credited at Seminole QF-1 wholesale (avoided cost) rate
ic_application_fee: Processing fee at co-op discretion (not stated); $60 net-meter trip fee
external_disconnect: Required all sizes (lockable manual disconnect, outside, accessible, separate from meter socket)
non_export_option: Stand-alone batteries (no RGS) may only charge from grid and may not interconnect/parallel; UL-listed automatic transfer switch required
storage_specific_notes: Agreement sec. 12 (2026): battery paired with RGS must be UL 1741 certified with meter placard "Battery storage utilized in this facility"; battery is solely for customer use and shall NOT export to the co-op; backup operation only when isolated (UL ATS or special inverter). Batteries are not renewable under Rule 25-6.065(2)(d); battery-only systems may charge from grid but may not interconnect (ATS required). So battery discharge never earns QF-1 credit and grid arbitrage via export is prohibited. Adding a battery is permitted under these guidelines; exceeding approved battery capacity is a disconnection ground, implying battery must be declared (new application for GPR changes 30 days ahead). No legacy retail NEM to lose.

rule_summary: Municipal (City of Lakeland); own Net Metering Service schedule Sheets 8.4-8.6 (eff. 2023-10-01). PV only (static inverters). Tiers: T1 <=10 kW, T2 <=100 kW (residential), T3 <=2 MW (commercial). Sizing: PV may not exceed 100% of annual consumption; >90% of transformer/service capacity at customer expense. Exports metered on separate register and credited at full retail; kWh credits carry forward on a moving 12-month window and expire unpaid at end of window (no annual cash-out); on termination accumulated credit paid at full retail. No aggregate cap currently (utility may limit). 12-month minimum term; city may terminate on 30 days notice. Insurance T2 up to $1M, T3 up to $2M, T1 recommended. Manual lockable visible load-break disconnect required all tiers. Standards cite IEEE 1547-2003/UL 1741 (2005). MANDATORY RATE: residential solar customers must take Rate RSD (Residential Service Demand): $14.45/mo + $6.69/kW billing demand less Value of Solar Credit $0.92/kW + 2.674c/kWh energy (eff. 2025-10-01); legacy pre-2016 RS solar customers moved to RSD from 2026-01-01.
nem_aggregate_cap: None currently (utility reserves right to limit)
export_credit_value: Full retail kWh credit (separate register); moving 12-month carryforward; unused credits forfeited (no cash-out) except full-retail payout on termination
ic_application_fee: Not stated; Interconnection Study Charge possible for Tier 2/3
external_disconnect: Required all tiers (manual, lockable, visible load-break)
standby_charge: Residential solar customers mandatorily billed on demand rate RSD ($6.69/kW billing demand, $0.92/kW Value of Solar Credit); standby service not permitted on RSD
storage_specific_notes: Net Metering schedule applies to PV arrays only; storage not addressed in tariff sheets read (program chunk cites an "Agreement for Parallel Connection of PV and/or ESS" -- not read). Mandatory demand rate (RSD) makes battery peak-shaving valuable for residential PV customers. Customer must notify city of any change to PV system; effect of adding a battery on net metering status: Unclear. Grid charging / battery export credit: Unclear.

rule_summary: Municipal; own Solar Net Metering Agreement (Rev 5, 08/02/2019) under s. 366.91(6) F.S., not FPSC 25-6.065 tiers. PV systems up to 100 kWac only (single agreement, no tiers); single-phase allowed up to 15 kWac, three-phase balanced above. No fee for application or net meter. Excess kWh credited at applicable retail tariff (city says full retail value incl. taxes) and carried forward on a rolling 12-month window; unused credits forfeited to the City at end of window, never paid. City retains RECs. Insurance: general liability >= $100,000 (homeowner policy may satisfy) for all sizes. Physical isolation: either a manual lockable load-break disconnect adjacent to meter, OR elect meter removal as the isolation means (no switch). City may terminate agreement on 30 days notice for any reason. Standards cited are dated (UL 1741, IEEE 929-2000, IEEE 1262-1995).
export_credit_value: Full retail kWh credit (rolling 12-month carryforward; unused credits forfeited, no cash-out)
external_disconnect: Owner's choice: manual lockable load-break disconnect adjacent to meter, OR allow City to pull the net meter as isolation (no switch needed)
storage_specific_notes: Agreement and application define the system as PV only (static inverter), but the application form has a 'Batteries (if applicable)' field, so PV+battery is interconnected under the same agreement. No rule on battery export credit or grid charging: Unclear. Adding a battery to an existing net-metered system: agreement sec. 3.D says the agreement TERMINATES upon any modification or alteration of the PV system and a new Solar Net Metering Agreement is required (sec. 4.A notice). Because terms are unchanged for new agreements (no legacy/successor split), re-signing should not lose export value, but whether a battery counts as a 'modification' is not stated -- treat as requiring a new agreement.

rule_summary: Municipal (City of Gainesville d/b/a GRU); own Agreement for Interconnection and Parallel Operation of Distributed Generation Resources (s. 366.91(6) F.S.), not FPSC 25-6.065. Tiers sized in kW DC (not AC): T1 <=10 kW DC, T2 >10-100 kW DC ($400 fee), T3 >100 kW-2 MW DC ($1,000 fee). NEM ENDED for new systems: GRU Authority resolution 2024-04-17 -- excess kWh now credited at GRU's current fuel adjustment rate (not retail); monthly credit rolls to next bill; annual calendar-year true-up converted to cash at GRU avoided cost price (GRU may change without notice). Existing (pre-change) solar customers reported unaffected (Secondary). Pre-application Letter of Intent / circuit capacity check required (approval valid 1 yr); GRU enforces circuit hosting limits. Technical review ~4-5 weeks. Lockable visible load-break 'Auxiliary Generation Disconnect' within 10 ft and on same wall as meter required. Telemetry at owner cost >=250 kW DC. Customer keeps RECs. Insurance: web page says T1 $100k, T2 $1M, T3 $2M; 2022 agreement text says T1 $100k, T2 $300k, T3 $1M (current 04/08/2024 agreement is image-only, not read).
export_credit_value: GRU fuel adjustment rate (~3.5c/kWh at April 2024 adoption, varies monthly); year-end balance cashed out at GRU avoided cost
ic_application_fee: Tier 1 $0; Tier 2 $400; Tier 3 $1,000 (non-refundable) + system impact study at customer cost if needed; $100 missed meter-set fee
ic_study_trigger_kw: Utility discretion (study if initial feasibility evaluation inconclusive; circuit capacity pre-check for all sizes)
external_disconnect: Required all tiers (manual, lockable, visible load-break, within 10 ft of meter, labeled 'Auxiliary Generation Disconnect')
storage_specific_notes: Agreement defines DGR as a renewable generation system; NEM web page and agreement do not mention batteries at all -- export credit for battery discharge, grid charging, and storage sizing all Unclear. Adding a battery to an existing system: agreement sec. 10.3 requires prompt notice of any modification changing configuration/rating/operation and GRU may audit before reconnection; sec. 9.1.5 lets GRU disconnect for unapproved modifications. Whether a battery retrofit moves a pre-April-2024 retail-NEM customer onto the fuel-rate credit is not stated: Unclear. With exports at ~fuel rate, storage self-consumption is the main value lever.

rule_summary: TVA LPC that has taken TVA's LPC flexibility (local generation) option: NES buys customer solar exports itself under its own NESolar programs (Guidelines eff. Oct 2024) rather than the customer contracting with TVA under DPP. NESolar Savings (behind-the-meter excess generation): on-site PV or PV+battery, <=250 kW DC, primary purpose serving on-site load, NES purchases of exported energy capped at 100% of annual site usage, minimum 50 kWh/month average excess; program cap 10 MW first-come. Exports paid a seasonal rate plus TVA Standard Service Total Monthly Fuel Cost (TMFC): summer (Jun-Sep) 3.069c, winter (Dec-Mar) 3.197c, transition 3.244c/kWh + TMFC. NESolar Connect (line-side, >=200 kW solar or >=80 kW other): buys 100% of output at 7.363c summer / 4.459c winter / 5.682c transition + TMFC; 35 MW program cap. No net metering. Application for Interconnection of Renewable Generation due >=60 days before operation; Interconnection and Operating Agreement required for every solar install; NES may require (at customer cost) Transmission Screen, System Impact Study, Facilities Study (>500 kW), Flexibility Device Kit. TVA Transmission Study possible 5-25 MVA. No capacity expansion without NES written approval.
nem_cap_res_kw: N/A (no NEM); NESolar Savings <=250 kW DC
nem_cap_nonres_kw: N/A (no NEM); NESolar Savings <=250 kW DC; NESolar Connect >=200 kW solar
nem_aggregate_cap: NESolar Savings 10 MW program max; NESolar Connect 35 MW initial program max (first-come, first-served); current subscription not published
export_credit_value: NESolar Savings (eff. Oct 2024): 3.069c/kWh Jun-Sep, 3.197c Dec-Mar, 3.244c Apr/May/Oct/Nov, each plus TVA TMFC for the month; bill credit. NESolar Connect: 7.363c / 4.459c / 5.682c + TMFC
ic_study_trigger_kw: Utility discretion (Transmission Screen / System Impact Study any size; Facilities Study >500 kW; TVA Transmission Study 5-25 MVA)
non_export_option: Behind-the-meter self-consumption without a NESolar agreement still requires the Interconnection and Operating Agreement; NES may require customer-purchased equipment that prevents generation flowing to the NES grid (per IOA)
storage_specific_notes: NESolar Savings explicitly eligible for 'solar PV with battery storage installation'; 'Energy Resource' definition includes a facility that stores energy produced by another Energy Resource. Purchase rates apply exclusively to solar-based generation (non-solar may get a separate technology-specific rate at NES discretion), so grid-charged battery export is not credited under program terms as written: grid charging treatment Unclear, crediting of grid-sourced energy likely No. Adding a battery to an existing NESolar system: 'No expansion of the capacity of an Energy Resource may occur without prior written approval of NES' -- battery retrofit needs NES approval; guideline amendments do not apply to previously approved resources, but no rule on whether a retrofit re-baselines the system. No net metering to lose.

utility_name: Memphis Light, Gas and Water Division
rule_summary: TVA LPC; follows TVA framework (no net metering -- MLGW all-requirements contract bars buying power from others; exports only via TVA DPP at avoided cost, paid by TVA direct deposit). MLGW-specific deviations: three interconnection options, all dual-metered with a separate generation meter: (A) Self-Generation -- excess flows to grid WITHOUT compensation; (B) DPP sell-all to TVA; (C) Self-Generation + DPP sell-excess. Options A and C carry a monthly Electric Service Availability charge (residential $14.40/mo; non-residential varies by rate, from $32.00/mo for GSA part 1; subject to change). Application fee: residential $250 + $5/kW, non-residential $500 + $5/kW (check only). Customer pays construction quote (generation meter + socket, meter labor, any upgrades, one System Acceptance Test); $200 per re-test ($200 initial test waived for TVA Green Connect QCN projects). Technical review ~4-5 weeks; interconnection study at MLGW discretion by size/location. Interconnection and Parallel Operation Agreement + liability insurance documentation required (amount not read).
export_credit_value: Self-Generation: $0 (excess uncompensated); with DPP: TVA avoided cost (see TN state row)
ic_application_fee: Residential $250 + $5/kW proposed; non-residential $500 + $5/kW; plus construction quote (generation meter, socket, upgrades, acceptance test); $200 per failed-test retest
non_export_option: No defined non-export path: Self-Generation option lets excess flow to grid uncompensated; still requires full application, separate generation meter and monthly availability charge
standby_charge: Electric Service Availability charge on Self-Generation customers (options A and C): residential $14.40/month; non-residential varies by rate schedule, from $32.00/month (GSA part 1); not charged for DPP sell-all (option B)
storage_specific_notes: Battery storage is explicitly allowed with Self-Generation and Self-Generation+DPP options; application collects battery make/model, kW AC and kWh AC per battery. MLGW recommends batteries to avoid uncompensated export. Whether grid-charged battery energy may be exported/sold under DPP is not addressed by MLGW (TVA DPP covers renewable QF output): Unclear. Adding a battery to an existing system: no MLGW rule found; since equipment is listed on the application/agreement, a retrofit likely needs a new application but this is not stated -- Unclear. No NEM status to lose.

rule_summary: TVA LPC; follows TVA framework (no net metering; excess sold only via TVA DPP up to 80 MW; KUB has no obligation to buy excess). KUB-specific terms: $500 application fee for any interconnection; Interconnection, Metering and Parallel Operation Agreement covers generating AND/OR storage systems ('Qualifying System', gross power rating in kW DC). Participant pays KUB actual costs incl. overheads: impact studies, installation verification, metering installation and meter O&M, upgrades, recurring periodic interconnection costs, and disconnection costs. Manual lockable visible load-break 'Generation and/or Storage Disconnect' adjacent to meter socket required with weatherproof single-line diagram. No insurance required (encouraged). Anti-islanding trip <10 cycles. Standards: latest IEEE 1547, UL 1741 SA, IEEE 519. No parallel operation until inspection, KUB site verification/commissioning witness and written authorization.
export_credit_value: None from KUB; excess only via TVA DPP (see TN state row)
ic_application_fee: $500 (any size) + KUB actual costs (studies, verification, metering, upgrades, periodic metering O&M)
ic_study_trigger_kw: Utility discretion (screening per KUB interconnection procedures; impact studies at participant expense)
external_disconnect: Required (manual, lockable, visible load-break, labeled 'Generation and/or Storage Disconnect', adjacent to meter socket)
storage_specific_notes: Agreement explicitly covers storage-only or generation+storage systems ('store, generate, and/or sell'); islanding definition names batteries. No rule on grid charging or on export of grid-charged energy (TVA DPP buys renewable QF output): Unclear. Adding a battery to an existing system: sec. 7.1 requires written notice >=60 calendar days before any modification that changes gross power rating OR changes any component; KUB may accept or deny, review/upgrade costs borne by participant, and no parallel operation of the modified system until KUB re-verification and written authorization. No NEM status to lose. Agreement read is the version at kub.org/uploads/KUB_Interconnection_Agreement_.pdf; KUB page now links a 2024 version (not read).

rule_summary: TVA LPC (north AL; APSC has no jurisdiction). Own Solar Connect program (TVA LPC flexibility): HU itself buys behind-the-meter excess generation as an itemized bill credit at a rate set each January from the TVA wholesale rate -- 6.427c/kWh for 2026 (vs TVA DPP avoided cost ~3.8c in TN state row). No net metering or net billing. Eligible: customer-owned solar <=50 kW on a single-meter installation, new systems and systems aging out of TVA programs; program has a participation cap (size not published). Alternatives: TVA DPP, or operate non-export (production-limiting design) with no payment. $100 application fee billed to account plus Aid-to-Construction payment for HU interconnection costs. Insurance: none <=10 kW; $1M general liability naming HU as additional insured >10 kW. Solar disconnect and main service disconnect must be grouped outside by the meter along with rapid-shutdown control. NABCEP-certified installer required to approve design and construction. Witness test by HU meter shop before permission to operate. Unauthorized exporting systems get 90 days to execute an interconnection agreement.

export_credit_value: Solar Connect 2026: 6.427c/kWh bill credit for excess energy (reset each January from TVA wholesale rate)
ic_application_fee: $100 (billed to account) + Aid-to-Construction payment for site-specific HU interconnection costs
external_disconnect: Required: solar disconnect grouped with main service overcurrent disconnect outside near meter (plus emergency rapid-shutdown control device)
non_export_option: Yes: systems designed so no excess flows to grid (production limited to instantaneous on-site load) are an explicit option; still need interconnection agreement/approval
storage_specific_notes: Batteries 'potentially allowed' with additional requirements: typically need mechanical open-transition throw-over (i.e. backup isolation) switches, extra documentation and testing; 'battery commutated systems cannot operate interconnected to the grid'. Combined with the single-meter rule and the ban on any separately derived source without written HU permission, grid-parallel battery export or grid charging for arbitrage looks restricted, but no explicit rule on grid charging: Unclear. Adding a battery to an existing Solar Connect/DPP system: requires HU approval (written permission for any separately derived source) and likely re-testing; whether it affects Solar Connect eligibility is not stated. No NEM to lose.
